blocks.text: Genesis 5 belongs to the opening movement of Genesis, where creation, genealogy, flood, and city-building appear within a broader ancient Near Eastern literary environment. Comparable traditions can illuminate shared motifs and cultural questions, but they do not by themselves prove that Genesis copied another account or determine how its claims should be interpreted. Questions about the book’s composition also remain disputed because Genesis does not narrate the history of its own formation.

Within the whole book, this genealogy stands in Genesis 1–11, the account of universal origins. Genesis later shifts in chapters 12–50 to the story of an ancestral family and closes with Jacob’s household in Egypt. Genesis 5 therefore forms part of the movement from humanity’s beginnings toward the family narratives that dominate the rest of the book.
